cards.title: Act Like You Belong
cards.instruction: You do not understand what is happening. Copy the confidence around you and never admit confusion.

cards.title: What Are We Now?
cards.instruction: Find out how someone defines the relationship without directly asking for a label.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've folded my towel beside yours. That's the visitor pile, is it? Should I put my washbag there too?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I folded mine because the hook broke. Your old towel is still on your hook.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course, the broken hook. Shall I use the old towel when I stay tonight?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Use it. I haven't given that space to anyone else.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: When I leave, do you want it back on my hook or with the guest laundry?

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 asks what towel pile is instead of confidently copying its presumed meaning; A3 and A5 indirectly test old place in household.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 broken hook and old towel support A3 overnight use; B4 retained space prompts A5 future storage.

relationship.evidence: B2 explains housekeeping and B4 reassures without naming relationship.

heightening.evidence: A5 tests whether B4 retained place extends beyond this visit.

specificity.evidence: A1 towel/washbag and B2 old hook ground former presence.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 guest laundry choice carries the relationship question concisely.
